t tests and Wilcoxon tests

Source: vignettes/articles/GLM_MEANS.rmd
GLM_MEANS.rmd

Description

This shows the output of mean comparison functions from the package rwf: report_ttests and report_wtests. Both functions run pairwise comparisons between the levels of each independent variable and return a table with test statistics, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and Bonferroni-adjusted significance flags.

  • Use report_ttests when data meet the normality assumption (parametric).
  • Use report_wtests when data are ordinal or normality cannot be assumed (non-parametric).

Installation instructions for rwf can be found here

The code can be found here

Data

The df_insurance dataset is used throughout this vignette. It contains insurance data for 1338 individuals with the following variables:

Format: A data frame with 1338 rows and 7 variables:

  • age: Age of the individual
  • sex: Sex of the individual (male/female)
  • bmi: Body Mass Index
  • children: Number of children covered by the insurance
  • smoker: Smoking status (yes/no)
  • region: Region of residence (southwest, southeast, northwest, northeast)
  • charges: Medical insurance charges billed

Source: researchpy repo

Assumptions

t-test

  • Independence: observations are independent within and between groups (Student, 1908). For a within-subjects design, the pairs are independent of each other.
  • Scale: the DV is measured on an interval or ratio scale.
  • Normality: the DV is normally distributed within each group; for a within-subjects design, the differences d_i are normally distributed (Student, 1908). With large groups the t-test is robust to non-normality. Normality can be checked with the Shapiro-Wilk test (Shapiro & Wilk, 1965).
  • Equal variances: Student’s t-test (var.equal = TRUE) assumes equal variances in both groups. Welch’s t-test (the default) does not (Welch, 1947) and is the safer default (Delacre et al., 2017). The Bartlett columns (k_squared[bartlett], df[bartlett], p[bartlett]) test this assumption (Bartlett, 1937); p[bartlett] < .05 suggests unequal variances. Bartlett’s test is itself sensitive to non-normality (Box, 1953).

Wilcoxon test

  • Independence: observations are independent within and between groups (Wilcoxon, 1945; Mann & Whitney, 1947). For a within-subjects design (signed-rank test), the pairs are independent of each other.
  • Scale: the DV is at least ordinal. For the signed-rank test, the differences d_i must be meaningful to rank, so the DV should be interval.
  • No normality required: the test uses ranks instead of raw values (Wilcoxon, 1945).
  • Shape: the rank-sum test compares whether values in one group tend to be larger than in the other, P(X_1>X_2)\neq 0.5 (Mann & Whitney, 1947). It can be read as a difference in medians only when both groups have the same distribution shape and spread; otherwise it can be significant even with equal medians (Fagerland & Sandvik, 2009). The signed-rank test assumes the differences d_i are symmetric around their median (Wilcoxon, 1945).
  • Ties: tied values are given average ranks and the variance is corrected for ties (see Formulas).

T-Test

report_ttests runs independent-samples t-tests for all pairwise combinations of levels of the specified independent variable(s) against a dependent variable. When multiple IVs are provided, it tests all level combinations.

The calls below demonstrate the key options:

  • Single IV (iv = 2, sex): one pairwise comparison (male vs. female).
  • Single IV (iv = 4, children): pairwise comparisons across all child-count groups.
  • Multiple IVs (iv = c(2,4)): all combinations of sex and children levels.
  • alternative: controls the direction of the hypothesis — "two.sided" (default), "less", or "greater".
  • var.equal = TRUE: uses Student’s t-test assuming equal variances; default (FALSE) uses Welch’s t-test which does not assume equal variances and is generally safer.
report_ttests(df=df_insurance,dv=7,iv=c(2))
##        DV  IV level1 level2  n1  n2         t      df          p      CI_l      CI_u alternative                  method    mean1    mean2     sd1      sd2 sd_pooled         d          r

##   k_squared[bartlett] df[bartlett]  p[bartlett] bonferroni_p significant
## 1            15.58524            1 7.886777e-05         0.05        TRUE

Explanation of columns

Column Effect Description Reference
DV dependent variable
IV independent variable
level1 level 1
level2 level 2
n1 sample size for level 1
n2 sample size for level 2
t t statistic
df degrees of freedom for t statistic
p p value
CI_l confidence interval lower bound
CI_u confidence interval upper bound
alternative alternative hypothesis
method name of method should be displayed here
mean1 mean for level 1
mean2 mean for level 2
sd1 standard deviation for level 1
sd2 standard deviation for level 2
sd_pooled pooled standard deviation combined standard deviation of both levels
d measure of effect size cohen’s d
d Very small 0.01 Sawilowsky (2009)
d Small 0.20 Cohen (1988)
d Medium 0.50 Cohen (1988)
d Large 0.80 Cohen (1988)
d Very large 1.20 Sawilowsky (2009)
d Huge 12.0 Sawilowsky (2009)
r measure of effect size correlation effect size
k_squared bartlett bartlett test for homogeneity of variances
df bartlett bartlett test for homogeneity of variances
p bartlett bartlett test for homogeneity of variances significant values indicate heteroscedasticity
bonferroni_p bonferroni adjusted critical value for a=0.05
significant if TRUE result is significant after bonferroni adjustment

Wilcoxon Test

report_wtests runs the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Mann-Whitney U), the non-parametric equivalent of the independent-samples t-test. It makes no assumption about the distribution of the data and compares group medians via rank ordering. Use it when the normality assumption is violated or the outcome is ordinal.

The calls mirror those in the T-Test section exactly, allowing direct comparison of parametric and non-parametric results on the same data. The key difference in the output is the W statistic (Wilcoxon rank-sum) in place of t.

report_wtests(df=df_insurance,dv=7,iv=c(2))
##        DV  IV level1 level2  n1  n2      W         p      CI_l     CI_u alternative                                            method    mean1    mean2     sd1      sd2 sd_pooled         d
## 1 charges sex female   male 662 676 221304 0.7286511 -929.0673 566.9229   two.sided Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction 12569.58 13956.75 11128.7 12971.03  12085.02 0.1147844
##             r k_squared[bartlett] df[bartlett]  p[bartlett] bonferroni_p significant
## 1 0.009484225            15.58524            1 7.886777e-05         0.05       FALSE

Explanation of columns

Column Effect Description Reference
DV dependent variable
IV independent variable
level1 level 1
level2 level 2
n1 sample size for level 1
n2 sample size for level 2
W wilcoxon statistic
df degrees of freedom for t statistic
p p value
CI_l confidence interval lower bound
CI_u confidence interval upper bound
alternative alternative hypothesis
method name of method should be displayed here
mean1 mean for level 1
mean2 mean for level 2
sd1 standard deviation for level 1
sd2 standard deviation for level 2
sd_pooled pooled standard deviation combined standard deviation of both levels
d measure of effect size cohen’s d
d Very small 0.01 Sawilowsky (2009)
d Small 0.20 Cohen (1988)
d Medium 0.50 Cohen (1988)
d Large 0.80 Cohen (1988)
d Very large 1.20 Sawilowsky (2009)
d Huge 12.0 Sawilowsky (2009)
r measure of effect size correlation effect size
k_squared bartlett bartlett test for homogeneity of variances
df bartlett bartlett test for homogeneity of variances
p bartlett bartlett test for homogeneity of variances significant values indicate heteroscedasticity
bonferroni_p bonferroni adjusted critical value for a=0.05
significant if TRUE result is significant after bonferroni adjustment

Formulas

Group 1 = level1, group 2 = level2; x_{1i} (i=1,\dots,n_1) and x_{2j} (j=1,\dots,n_2) are the DV values of the complete cases in each group, g_i is the IV value of case i; N=n_1+n_2; \alpha=0.05; m = number of rows in the output table; \Phi, \varphi = standard normal CDF and density, z_q=\Phi^{-1}(q); t_{q,\,df} = q quantile of the t distribution.

report_ttests

n1, n2

n_1=\sum_i \mathbf{1}[g_i=\text{level1}],\qquad n_2=\sum_i \mathbf{1}[g_i=\text{level2}]

mean1, mean2

\bar{x}_1=\frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}x_{1i},\qquad \bar{x}_2=\frac{1}{n_2}\sum_{j=1}^{n_2}x_{2j}

sd1, sd2

s_1=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n_1-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}(x_{1i}-\bar{x}_1)^2},\qquad s_2=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n_2-1}\sum_{j=1}^{n_2}(x_{2j}-\bar{x}_2)^2}

t

\text{Welch (default):}\quad t=\frac{\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2}{SE},\qquad SE=\sqrt{\frac{s_1^2}{n_1}+\frac{s_2^2}{n_2}}

\text{Student (var.equal = TRUE):}\quad t=\frac{\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2}{SE},\qquad SE=s_p\sqrt{\frac{1}{n_1}+\frac{1}{n_2}},\qquad s_p^2=\frac{(n_1-1)s_1^2+(n_2-1)s_2^2}{N-2}

df

\text{Welch:}\quad df=\frac{\left(\frac{s_1^2}{n_1}+\frac{s_2^2}{n_2}\right)^2}{\frac{(s_1^2/n_1)^2}{n_1-1}+\frac{(s_2^2/n_2)^2}{n_2-1}},\qquad \text{Student:}\quad df=N-2

p

p_{\text{two.sided}}=2\,P(T_{df}\ge\lvert t\rvert),\qquad p_{\text{less}}=P(T_{df}\le t),\qquad p_{\text{greater}}=P(T_{df}\ge t),\qquad T_{df}\sim t(df)

CI_l, CI_u

\text{two.sided:}\quad \left[(\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2)-t_{1-\alpha/2,\,df}\,SE,\ \ (\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2)+t_{1-\alpha/2,\,df}\,SE\right]

\text{less:}\quad \left(-\infty,\ \ (\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2)+t_{1-\alpha,\,df}\,SE\right],\qquad \text{greater:}\quad \left[(\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2)-t_{1-\alpha,\,df}\,SE,\ \ \infty\right)

sd_pooled

s_{pooled}=\sqrt{\frac{s_1^2+s_2^2}{2}}

d

d=\frac{\lvert\bar{x}_2-\bar{x}_1\rvert}{s_{pooled}}

r

r=\frac{d}{\sqrt{d^2+\frac{N^2}{n_1n_2}}}

k_squared[bartlett]

K^2=\frac{(N-2)\ln s_p^2-(n_1-1)\ln s_1^2-(n_2-1)\ln s_2^2}{1+\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{n_1-1}+\frac{1}{n_2-1}-\frac{1}{N-2}\right)},\qquad s_p^2=\frac{(n_1-1)s_1^2+(n_2-1)s_2^2}{N-2}

df[bartlett]

df_{bartlett}=k-1=2-1=1

p[bartlett]

p_{bartlett}=P\left(\chi^2_{1}\ge K^2\right)

bonferroni_p

\alpha_{bonferroni}=\frac{\alpha}{m}=\frac{0.05}{m}

significant

\text{significant}=\begin{cases}\text{TRUE} & p<\alpha_{bonferroni}\\ \text{FALSE} & p\ge\alpha_{bonferroni}\end{cases}

report_wtests

n1, n2, mean1, mean2, sd1, sd2, sd_pooled, d, k_squared[bartlett], df[bartlett], p[bartlett], bonferroni_p, significant: as in report_ttests.

W

W=R_1-\frac{n_1(n_1+1)}{2},\qquad R_1=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}\operatorname{rank}(x_{1i})\ \ \text{(ranks in the pooled sample of } N \text{ values, ties averaged)}

p

\text{exact } (n_1<50,\ n_2<50)\text{:}\quad p_{\text{two.sided}}=\min\{1,\ 2P(W_0\le W),\ 2P(W_0\ge W)\},\qquad p_{\text{less}}=P(W_0\le W),\qquad p_{\text{greater}}=P(W_0\ge W)

\text{normal approximation (otherwise):}\quad p_{\text{two.sided}}=2\min\{\Phi(z),\ 1-\Phi(z)\},\qquad p_{\text{less}}=\Phi(z),\qquad p_{\text{greater}}=1-\Phi(z)

z=\frac{W-\frac{n_1n_2}{2}-c}{\sigma_W},\qquad \sigma_W=\sqrt{\frac{n_1n_2}{12}\left[(N+1)-\frac{\sum_k(t_k^3-t_k)}{N(N-1)}\right]},\qquad c=\begin{cases}0.5\,\operatorname{sign}\left(W-\frac{n_1n_2}{2}\right) & \text{two.sided}\\ 0.5 & \text{greater}\\ -0.5 & \text{less}\end{cases}

W_0 = null distribution of W (conditional on the ties), t_k = number of values in tie group k.

CI_l, CI_u

\text{exact, no ties:}\quad \text{two.sided: }\left[D_{(k)},\ D_{(n_1n_2-k+1)}\right],\quad \text{greater: }\left[D_{(k)},\ \infty\right),\quad \text{less: }\left(-\infty,\ D_{(n_1n_2-k+1)}\right]

k=\min\{w:\ P(W_0\le w)>\alpha/2\}\ \text{(two.sided)},\qquad k=\min\{w:\ P(W_0\le w)>\alpha\}\ \text{(one-sided)}

\text{normal approximation:}\quad \text{two.sided: } z(CI_l)=z_{1-\alpha/2},\ z(CI_u)=z_{\alpha/2},\qquad \text{greater: } z(CI_l)=z_{1-\alpha},\qquad \text{less: } z(CI_u)=z_{\alpha}

D_{(1)}\le\dots\le D_{(n_1n_2)} = sorted differences x_{1i}-x_{2j}; z(\Delta) = z computed on x_{1i}-\Delta and x_{2j}.

r

r=\frac{\lvert Z\rvert}{\sqrt{N}},\qquad Z=\Phi^{-1}\left(1-\frac{p}{2}\right)

Between- and within-subjects designs

Between subjects: two independent groups, x_{1i} (i=1,\dots,n_1) and x_{2j} (j=1,\dots,n_2), N=n_1+n_2. Within subjects: n paired observations (x_{1i},x_{2i}) on the same cases, d_i=x_{1i}-x_{2i} (i=1,\dots,n).

t-test

Between subjects (independent samples)

\text{Welch:}\quad t=\frac{\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2}{\sqrt{\frac{s_1^2}{n_1}+\frac{s_2^2}{n_2}}},\qquad df=\frac{\left(\frac{s_1^2}{n_1}+\frac{s_2^2}{n_2}\right)^2}{\frac{(s_1^2/n_1)^2}{n_1-1}+\frac{(s_2^2/n_2)^2}{n_2-1}}

\text{Student:}\quad t=\frac{\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2}{s_p\sqrt{\frac{1}{n_1}+\frac{1}{n_2}}},\qquad s_p^2=\frac{(n_1-1)s_1^2+(n_2-1)s_2^2}{N-2},\qquad df=N-2

d=\frac{\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2}{s_p}

Within subjects (paired samples)

\bar{d}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}d_i,\qquad s_d=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(d_i-\bar{d})^2},\qquad SE=\frac{s_d}{\sqrt{n}}

t=\frac{\bar{d}}{s_d/\sqrt{n}},\qquad df=n-1

p_{\text{two.sided}}=2\,P(T_{n-1}\ge\lvert t\rvert),\qquad p_{\text{less}}=P(T_{n-1}\le t),\qquad p_{\text{greater}}=P(T_{n-1}\ge t)

\text{two.sided: }\left[\bar{d}-t_{1-\alpha/2,\,n-1}\,SE,\ \ \bar{d}+t_{1-\alpha/2,\,n-1}\,SE\right],\qquad \text{less: }\left(-\infty,\ \bar{d}+t_{1-\alpha,\,n-1}\,SE\right],\qquad \text{greater: }\left[\bar{d}-t_{1-\alpha,\,n-1}\,SE,\ \infty\right)

d_z=\frac{\bar{d}}{s_d}=\frac{t}{\sqrt{n}}

Wilcoxon test

Between subjects (rank-sum test, Mann-Whitney U)

W=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}\operatorname{rank}(x_{1i})-\frac{n_1(n_1+1)}{2}\ \ \text{(ranks in the pooled sample of } N \text{ values)},\qquad E(W)=\frac{n_1n_2}{2}

z=\frac{W-\frac{n_1n_2}{2}-c}{\sqrt{\frac{n_1n_2}{12}\left[(N+1)-\frac{\sum_k(t_k^3-t_k)}{N(N-1)}\right]}},\qquad r=\frac{\lvert Z\rvert}{\sqrt{N}}

\text{CI: Hodges-Lehmann, from the sorted } n_1n_2 \text{ differences } x_{1i}-x_{2j}

Within subjects (signed-rank test)

V=\sum_{i:\,d_i>0}\operatorname{rank}\left(\lvert d_i\rvert\right),\qquad E(V)=\frac{n'(n'+1)}{4}

\text{exact } (n<50)\text{:}\quad p_{\text{two.sided}}=\min\{1,\ 2P(V_0\le V),\ 2P(V_0\ge V)\},\qquad p_{\text{less}}=P(V_0\le V),\qquad p_{\text{greater}}=P(V_0\ge V)

\text{normal approximation (otherwise):}\quad z=\frac{V-\frac{n'(n'+1)}{4}-c}{\sigma_V},\qquad \sigma_V=\sqrt{\frac{n'(n'+1)(2n'+1)}{24}-\frac{\sum_k(t_k^3-t_k)}{48}}

p_{\text{two.sided}}=2\min\{\Phi(z),\ 1-\Phi(z)\},\qquad p_{\text{less}}=\Phi(z),\qquad p_{\text{greater}}=1-\Phi(z)

\text{exact, no ties or zeros:}\quad \text{two.sided: }\left[A_{(k)},\ A_{(M-k+1)}\right],\quad \text{greater: }\left[A_{(k)},\ \infty\right),\quad \text{less: }\left(-\infty,\ A_{(M-k+1)}\right],\qquad M=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}

k=\min\{v:\ P(V_0\le v)>\alpha/2\}\ \text{(two.sided)},\qquad k=\min\{v:\ P(V_0\le v)>\alpha\}\ \text{(one-sided)}

r=\frac{\lvert Z\rvert}{\sqrt{n}},\qquad Z=\Phi^{-1}\left(1-\frac{p}{2}\right)

n' = number of non-zero d_i (zero differences are dropped in the normal approximation; the exact test ranks all n differences and conditions V_0 on their ranks), t_k = number of \lvert d_i\rvert in tie group k, c = continuity correction (0.5\,\operatorname{sign}(V-E(V)) two.sided, 0.5 greater, -0.5 less), A_{(1)}\le\dots\le A_{(M)} = sorted Walsh averages (d_i+d_j)/2, i\le j.
